editorial:
Imagine flying all the way to England for your parents' funeral, only to find out that something feels completely wrong. You are stepped into the shoes of a daughter who just cannot accept the official story that her parents died of natural causes. The vibe is very tense because you feel her frustration as she tries to uncover the truth. She starts to suspect the nurse who looked after them, but there is a big problem: the whole town loves this nurse. It feels like a game of cat and mouse where the main character is the only one seeing the red flags while everyone else tells her she is just grieving.

What really works here is the slow build of dread and the way the mystery unfolds. The acting is solid, and while the pace starts slow, it picks up once the killer realizes the daughter is getting too close to the truth. If you like old-school mysteries where the hero is isolated and scared, you will love this one. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you want the best picture quality available for a classic.
endingExplained: The tension peaks when the nurse finally tries to kill the daughter, just like she did to the parents. After a scary struggle, the truth comes out that the nurse was poisoning them for money. The daughter manages to fight back and survive the attack. In the end, the police arrive and the nurse is caught, proving that the daughter was right all along. The mystery closes with justice being served and the truth revealed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old mysteries and whodunits.
